title: WPSB/287/2019 of DEVENDRA SINGH BORA Vs STATE OF UTTARAKHAND

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND
 AT NAINITAL
ON THE 8TH DAY OF OCTOBER, 2021
BEFORE:
HON'BLE SHRI JUSTICE MANOJ KUMAR TIWARI
AND
HON'BLE SHRI JUSTICE ALOK KUMAR VERMA
WRIT PETITION (S/B) No. 287 of 2019
BETWEEN:
Devendra Singh Bora ....Petitioner
AND:
State of Uttarakhand
and others ....Respondents
With
WRIT PETITION (S/B) No. 6 of 2020
 WRIT PETITION (S/B) No. 286 of 2019
(By Mr. Pradeep Kumar Chauhan, Mr. Ganesh Kandpal,
Mr. Vinay Kumar and Mr. M.S. Bhandari, Advocate holding
brief of Mr. Alok Dalalkoti, Advocates for the petitioners.
(By Mr. Pradeep Joshi, Additional Chief Standing Counsel
for the State)
This Writ Petition coming on for hearing this day,
Hon'ble Shri Justice Manoj Kumar Tiwari, J. delivered the
following Judgment:
JUDGEMENT

Since common questions of fact and law are
involved in these writ petitions, therefore they are clubbed
together and are being heard & decided together. However,

2
for the sake of convenience, facts of WPSB No. 287 of 2019
are being considered.
2. The relief sought in WPSB No. 287 of 2019 is
reproduced below:-

"1- a writ order or direction in the nature of
mandamus or any other writ declaring the Rule
6 of the Uttarakhand Subordinate offices clerical
cadre employees (direct recruitment) Rule,
2004 as well as the amendment made thereto
by virtue of notification dated 13.8.2013 so far
it provides the 10% quota for Intermediate pass
class IV employees and 15% Quota for high
school pass class IV employee, as null and
void."
3. Petitioners are Group-D employees serving in
School Education Department of Uttarakhand Government.
Academic qualification needed for appointment on Group-D
post is High School; while, petitioners possess higher
qualification. As per applicable service Rules, Group-D
employees are eligible for promotion against Group-C posts
in ministerial cadre. State Government has framed the
Subordinate Offices Ministerial Staff (Direct Recruitment)
Rules, 2004, which were notified on 14.06.2004. Rule 6 of
the aforesaid Rules is reproduced below:-
"6- Source of Recruitment- Recruitment to the
lowest grade of the ministerial staff in a
subordinate office shall be made by direct
recruitment through the Selection Committee
referred in Rule 17 on the basis of academic
and other attainments as provided in Rule 9:
Provided that up to 25 percent of the vacancies
in a particular subordinate office may be filled
by the Appointing Authority by promotion
amongst 15 percent from amongst High School
pass and 10 percent from Intermediate pass
Group D employees of that office in accordance
with the orders of Government issued from time
to time."

3
4. Petitioners are aggrieved by that part of proviso
to Rule 6, which carves out a separate quota for promotion
to High School pass employees within the 25% quota
available to persons serving on Group-D posts. A perusal of
Rule 6 reveals that recruitment to the lowest grade in
ministerial cadre has to be made by direct recruitment,
however, proviso to Rule 6 lays down that upto 25%
vacancies in the ministerial cadre may be filled by
promoting Group-D employees. The proviso then bifurcates
the promotion quota vacancies based on academic
qualification, namely, 15% vacancies would be set apart for
High School Pass Group-D employees and the remaining
10% vacancies would be available to be supplied by
promoting Intermediate pass Group-D employees.
5. This compartmentalization of vacancies based
on academic qualification has been challenged by the
petitioners as arbitrary and unjust.
6. Learned counsel for the petitioners submits that
this amounts to artificial classification amongst Group-D
employees, who constitute a homogeneous class of
employees.
7. The challenge thrown by petitioners to proviso
to Rule 6 of the aforesaid Rules is without any substance.
In Government service, conditions of service are determined
by statutory rules framed under proviso to Article 309 of the
Constitution and in exercise of its rule making power, State
Government can amend or repeal the service rules, thereby
altering the conditions of service. A Government servant
does not have a vested right of promotion and the only right
he has, is right to be considered for promotion in terms of
the service rules. The State Government is well within its

4
right to prescribe separate quota for promotion for different
category of employees.
8. Now the question arises whether Group-D
employees serving in Education Department can be further
classified based on their academic qualification. This
question is no longer res-integra. Qualification based
classification has been held to be valid. Hon'ble Supreme
Court in the case of V. Markendeya v. State of A.P.,
reported in (1989) 3 SCC 191 has held that differentiation
amongst graduate and non-graduate supervisors for the
purpose of pay scale is not violative of Article 14 and 16.
Similarly, in the case of Government of Andhra Pradesh v.
Dilip Kumar, reported in (1993) 2 SCC 210, Hon'ble
Supreme Court has upheld classification on the basis of
higher educational qualification in the matter of promotion.
9. Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of T.R.
Kothandaraman and others v. Tamil Nadu Water Supply &
Drainage BD and others, reported in (1994) 6 SCC 282,
after considering various decisions has summarized the
legal position in paragraph no. 16 of the judgment, which is
extracted below:-
"6. From what has been stated above, the
following legal propositions emerge
regarding educational qualification being a
basis of classification relating to promotion in
public service:
(1) Higher educational qualification is a
permissible basis of classification,
acceptability of which will depend on the
facts and circumstances of each case.
(2) Higher educational qualification can be
the basis not only for barring promotion, but
also for restricting the scope of promotion.

5
(3) Restriction placed cannot however go to
the extent of seriously jeopardising the
chances of promotion. To decide this, the
extent of restriction shall have also to be
looked into to ascertain whether it is
reasonable. Reasons for this are being
indicated later."
10. Respondents have contended that before State
reorganization, rules framed in the year 1975 by State of
Uttar Pradesh were holding the field and in the said rules
namely, U.P. Subordinate Offices Ministerial Staff (Direct
Recruitment) Rules, 1975, a separate 10% promotion quota
was available to High School pass Group-D employees,
which was later enhanced to 15%, under the new Rules
framed in the year 1985.
11. Learned Additional Chief Standing Counsel
appearing for the State has drawn our attention to
paragraph no. 14 of the counter affidavit, where the reason
for providing separate promotion quota to High School pass
Group-D employees has been mentioned. It is stated that
earlier academic qualification needed for appointment on
Group-D posts was only class-5 and now Group-D posts
have been declared to be dying cadre; in the absence of
separate quota for promotion, Group-D employees having
only High School qualification, would never be promoted
and they will have to stagnate on the same post, therefore
to ameliorate their condition, separate promotion quota was
provided to them. In paragraph no. 11 of the counter
affidavit, it has been stated that Rule 6 of the aforesaid
Rules was amended in the year 2013 and by the said
amendment, it was provided that if no High School pass
Group-D employee is available for promotion, then the
vacancies made available to them, can be supplied by
promoting more qualified Group-D employees. The

6
notification dated 13.08.2013, whereby Rule 6 of the
aforesaid Rules was amended, is on record as Annexure-1
to WPSB No. 06 of 2020.
12. Historically, candidates, who had studied upto
5th standard, were eligible for appointment on a Group-D
post and subsequently, the qualification needed for
appointment to Group-D posts was enhanced to 10th
standard. Thus, in order to protect the right of High School
pass employees, State Government in its wisdom, provided
separate promotion quota for them to ensure that chances
of promotion given to Group-D employees are not eaten
away by candidates having Intermediate or higher academic
qualification.
13. From the stand taken in the counter affidavit, it
is apparent that separate promotion quota made available
to High School pass candidates is not without purpose.
Since after passing High School (10th standard), a person
becomes educationally qualified for appointment on a
Group-D post; while persons, possessing higher
qualification, are also appointed on Group-D post, therefore,
in order to protect the interest of High School pass
candidates, State Government has provided separate
promotion quota to High School pass candidates to ensure
that they do not suffer stagnation. This, in our view, would
be a valid classification. It is settled position in law that
unequals cannot be treated equally.
14. In such view of the matter, the challenge
thrown by the petitioners to proviso to Rule 6 of the
aforesaid service Rules is without any substance.

7
15. Learned counsel for the petitioners then
submitted that, even after amendment in the rules made in
the year 2013, petitioners are not being considered for
promotion against vacancies earmarked for High School
pass Group-D employees despite non-availability of eligible
candidates.
16. In such view of the matter, the writ petitions
are disposed of with a direction to the respondents to
determine the number of vacancies available for promotion
to High School pass candidates and to hold promotion
exercise for supplying such vacancies from eligible
candidates. If eligible candidates are not available for
supplying such vacancies, then petitioners may be
considered for promotion against such vacancies. We hope
and expect that necessary exercise for supplying such
vacancies shall be completed within six months from today.
 (ALOK KUMAR VERMA, J.)
 (MANOJ KUMAR TIWARI, J.)
Shubham
